newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea says Sudan plotted to assassinate president.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea says Sudan plotted to assassinate president.

text.p: Eritrean Foreign Minister Haile Woldensae on Monday accused Sudan's Islamic-backed military government of plotting to kill Eritrea President Isaias Afewerki late last year.

The minister told a news conference that Khartoum had planned to carry out the assassination plot in November last year through an agent it had infiltrated into the ranks of the exiled National Democratic Alliance (NDA) of Sudan.
The Asmara-based NDA is made up of Sudanese rebel groups in exile fighting to overthrow the government in Khartoum.

"The NIF (National Islamic Front) regime in Khartoum plotted to assassinate Isaias Afewerki, dispatching a member of its foreign security forces to Asmara on November 14, 1996 to infiltrate the NDA of the Sudan so as to accomplish the abominable act," Haile said.
He said the Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir and spiritual leader Hassan al-Turabi were directly involved in the plot.

"This heinous crime was conceived at the highest levels of the NIF regime, with explicit orders given to the terrorist from senior government officials including Turabi and General Omar Al-Bashir, head of state," said Haile.

"The NIF's incontrovertible involvement in a heinous plot to assassinate yet another head of state is an additional testimony to the boundless limits that this rogue regime is prepared to take to pursue its objectives of subversion, terror and destabilisation," Haile added.
Haile said the tiny Red Sea state would file a complaint with the United Nations.
The minister named the would-be-assassin as Captain Nesredin Babakar Aba Al Khairat. Reporters were later given a transcript of Khairat's alleged confession by NDA security officials.

In the transcript, the accused tells of his military training in Sudan and that he left Khartoum on November 14, 1996, to go the Eritrean border in order to infiltrate the Sudanese opposition alliance.
According to the transcript, the suspect said that he was given the following order from the Administration of Security Service in Sudan:

"You will be going to Eritrea with a group whose members are 34 and with you 35. The mission of the group is to infiltrate the Alliance Forces and your responsibility is to put what you have learned into practice."
"After a while they explained that my mission was to eliminate Afwerki," Khairat says in the confession.
Haile said Khairat was being held by the NDA, which also includes veteran guerrilla leader John Garang's Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The SPLA has been fighting the government for almost 13 years for autonomy of the mostly Christian and animist south.

"The NDA uncovered the plot, and he (the suspect) is in the hands of the NDA," Haile added. The minister could not say why it took the authorities and the NDA so long to uncover the plot. He also did not say when the suspect was arrested.

The NDA has its headquarters in Asmara, the Eritrean capital. Eritrea, Sudan's small but militarily powerful eastern neighbour, backs the opposition but denies its army is taking part in the fighting.
